headline: The dollar is getting a hawkish-Fed lift and USD/JPY is trading above every short-term average, so a small buy on a dip toward 158.72 has room to push to 159.

messages.text: Hi all! The idea is to buy USD/JPY, which means betting the US dollar gets stronger against the Japanese yen. Price is about 158.79 right now.

The dollar has a reason to rise today. US inflation came in hotter than expected, and traders now talk about the Fed (the US central bank) raising rates by a bigger step. Higher US rates make the dollar more attractive.
The dollar index, a score of the dollar against a basket of currencies, is up 0.7% today and trending up. It is like the whole team running forward, not just one player.

On the 1-hour chart price sits above its 9, 21 and 50-period averages, and its RSI, a 0-100 score of how hard price has been pushed up, is 76. That means buyers are in control, though it also means price has run a bit already.

So I do not want to chase. I would place a buy order a little lower, around 158.72, with the exit if wrong at 158.55, just under a spot where price has turned 3 times before. First goal is 158.83, just under today's high of 158.85, then 159.00.

Honest note: the desk's odds test says there is no strong edge right now, and that test used a different, tighter plan. Mine is small and has no big event inside the window. Take it only if you accept that.

argument:
The case is momentum plus a fundamental push. US CPI surprised hot and Fed Governor Waller warned of a larger hike, and FXStreet shows the dollar rising against GBP, EUR, AUD and CAD on it. The dollar index is +0.7% today and in an uptrend. On USD/JPY itself, the 1h chart shows EMA9 (158.56) above EMA21 (158.34) above SMA50 (158.18) above SMA200 (158.01), RSI 76.2 and a positive MACD histogram. The 15m RSI is 70.2. The 5m chart is only mildly positive (RSI 58.8, MACD histogram slightly negative), which is why I propose buying a small dip rather than the live price.

The levels: price has already cleared Pivot R2 (158.686) and the 3x swing high at 158.574. Those old ceilings now act as floors. I put the entry at 158.72 and the stop at 158.55, just beneath the 3x swing high at 158.574 (about 1.1 ATR on the 1h chart, where ATR is the average hourly range of 0.159). Target 1 is 158.83, just before today's high at 158.847. Target 2 is 159.00, a round number; the levels file has no listed ceiling above today's high, and the 52-week high is 163.98, far away.

Risks I accept: RSI on the 1h chart is stretched, the optimizer says NO_EDGE (best plan 26% target-first, -0.09R, using a plain 1 ATR stop), the 10-year US yield is spiking (+3.1%), which can reverse fast, and the Tokyo session could bring Japan-side headlines. The event guard is CLEAR, and volatility is NORMAL (0.85x usual). The plan keeps the stop just beyond a real level and uses a limit order for a better entry.

plan.risk_reward: about 1:0.6 to target 1 and 1:1.6 to target 2

plan_plain: Place a buy order at about 158.72 on a dip. If price falls to 158.55, sell to limit the loss. Take some profit near 158.83, just under today's high, and the rest near 159.00. Winning about 1.6 for every 1 risked is the best case, and the code-checked odds are weak, so size small.
